title: Two-source extraction at log n plus constant entropy
formal:
Does there exist an integer \(C\ge0\) and one uniform deterministic polynomial-time algorithm \(A\) defining functions
\[
E_n:\{0,1\}^n\times\{0,1\}^n\longrightarrow\{0,1\}\qquad(n\ge1)
\]
such that, for every \(n\) and every two independent probability distributions \(X,Y\) on \(\{0,1\}^n\) with
\[
H_\infty(X),H_\infty(Y)\ge\log_2 n+C,
\]
we have
\[
\left|\Pr[E_n(X,Y)=1]-\frac12\right|\le\frac1{100}?
\]
The algorithm receives only \(n\) and the two strings. The same additive constant, finite program and polynomial running-time bound must work for all lengths and all eligible distributions.
definitions:
Write \(S_n=\{0,1\}^n\) for all binary strings of length \(n\). A probability distribution on this finite set is any function \(p:S_n\to[0,1]\) with real values and \(\sum_xp(x)=1\). Its min-entropy is
\[
H_\infty(p)=-\log_2\!\left(\max_{x\in S_n}p(x)\right).
\]
Thus the required entropy condition means \(p(x)\le 1/(2^C n)\) for every string \(x\). Distributions need not be uniform on their support, rational, computable or efficiently samplable. Independence means that the joint distribution is \(\Pr[X=x,Y=y]=p(x)q(y)\). The output probability in the question is the finite sum
\[
\Pr[E_n(X,Y)=1]=\sum_{x,y\in S_n}p(x)q(y)\,\mathbf1_{\{E_n(x,y)=1\}}.
\]
The indicator is one when its subscripted condition holds and zero otherwise. For a single output bit, the displayed bias is its statistical distance from the uniform bit, where statistical distance between distributions \(r,s\) on a finite set is \(\frac12\sum_z|r(z)-s(z)|\). There is no conditioning on either source in this guarantee.

Computation uses a deterministic multitape Turing machine with a fixed finite program and fixed finite tape alphabet. Its read-only input is \(1^n\#x\#y\), where \(|x|=|y|=n\), and its work tapes initially contain blanks. One transition reads and writes at most one symbol on each tape and moves each tape head by at most one cell, costing one step. There are no random coins, oracle calls, auxiliary seed, advice or length-dependent precomputed tables. The machine must halt and output exactly one bit on every such input. There must be integers \(K,d\ge1\) such that this takes at most \(K(n+1)^d\) transitions for all \(n,x,y\), including inputs at lengths with no eligible sources. The input contains no distribution description or samples other than \(x,y\); \(C,K,d\) and the machine are fixed existential choices, independent of both distributions and of \(n\). Let \(\mathcal A\) be the class of all machines meeting this total polynomial-time evaluation condition, and write \(E^A_n\) for the function computed by a member \(A\).

Only the probability bound concerns the random choice of the two input strings; the evaluator itself is deterministic. When \(\log_2n+C>n\), no eligible distribution exists, so the extraction requirement at that length is vacuous. Using a nonnegative integer for the existential additive constant fixes a harmless convention: any fixed real constant can be increased to such an integer. The task has one output bit and fixed error \(1/100\); it does not demand arbitrarily small error, more output bits or resilience to tampering.

context_blocks.text: Li’s introduction and concluding open questions explicitly distinguish the optimal additive threshold \(\log_2n+O(1)\) from the achieved asymptotic order \(O(\log n)\). This card retains its existing one-bit, error-\(1/100\), uniform polynomial-time version of that question; it does not interpret the paper’s title as claiming the additive threshold.

The source records nonconstructive existence at \(\log_2n+O(1)\). Its Theorem 1.6 gives polynomial-time extraction for every fixed positive constant error when each source has at least \(c\log_2n\) entropy for a suitable fixed \(c>1\), even when the two sources’ bits are interleaved. The remaining distinction is the coefficient of the logarithm.

Extraction from arbitrary independent sources is stronger than merely requiring a function to take both values on every sufficiently large Cartesian product. The latter property is a two-source disperser and yields a bipartite Ramsey graph. The fixed small-bias guarantee here requires approximate balance, not only nonconstancy.

Li and Zhong’s 2024 construction adds resistance to separate tampering of the sources. Its constant-error, one-bit theorem still has an entropy requirement \(c\log n\), with a constant \(c>1\); it does not assert the additive threshold.

Oh and Shaltiel’s July 2026 revision constructs extractors under a computational hardness assumption for distributions generated by small circuits. It concerns a restricted source class and a conditional result, whereas the present target is unconditional and covers arbitrary independent distributions.

why: The additive threshold asks whether polynomial-time evaluation can match the entropy scale available without an efficiency restriction, including its leading coefficient. It is a basic question about converting two independent imperfect sources into a nearly unbiased bit and has consequences for explicit Ramsey constructions.
answer_criterion:
Give a complete mathematically correct Lean proof of the existence proposition, including one finite machine, its uniform polynomial-time bound and the probability guarantee for all eligible distributions. Alternatively, give a complete Lean proof of its logical negation: for every integer \(C\ge0\) and every \(A\in\mathcal A\), there exist \(n\ge1\) and distributions \(p,q\) on \(S_n\), each having min-entropy at least \(\log_2n+C\), for which
\[
\left|\sum_{x,y\in S_n}p(x)q(y)\mathbf1_{\{E^A_n(x,y)=1\}}-\frac12\right|>\frac1{100}.
\]
In this negation the length and distributions may depend on the machine and additive constant. A construction requiring \(c\log_2n\) entropy for an unspecified constant \(c>1\), nonuniform existence alone, or a conditional implication does not establish the displayed unconditional target.

references.title: Extractors for Samplable Distributions from the Two-Source Extractor Recipe
references.locator: ECCC TR25-107, revision 3 posted 14 July 2026, following STOC 2026. Abstract and Section 1, especially Theorem 1.2, printed p. 4 / PDF p. 8, and its subsequent comparison: conditional extraction from circuit-samplable distributions, not the unrestricted two-source target. The first report appeared 30 July 2025.

progress.text: Li’s revised preprint proves explicit two-source extraction at entropy \(c\log n\) for a suitable constant \(c>1\), and separately lists \(\log n+O(1)\) as an open question.
Li and Zhong give explicit non-malleable extraction at logarithmic entropy with a multiplicative constant; the one-bit additive-threshold question is not settled.
Oh and Shaltiel’s third revision treats circuit-samplable distributions under a hardness assumption. Its theorem does not resolve unconditional extraction from arbitrary pairs of sources.

sentences: Two arbitrary independent distributions on n-bit strings each have min-entropy at least log base two of n plus one fixed additive constant.
The question asks for one deterministic polynomial-time algorithm that turns one string from each source into a bit with bias at most one hundredth.
The same program and time bound must work at every length without an extra seed, advice or descriptions of the distributions.
Li’s checked theorem achieves a constant multiple of log n entropy, while his source explicitly leaves the additive threshold as a further question.
Matching that threshold efficiently would sharpen a central randomness-extraction result and have consequences for explicit Ramsey graphs.

checked_sources: Read the complete canonical TCS-7271 record and preserved its previously admitted 1/100-error specialization. The primary open question does not numerically fix its constant error; the card explicitly retains that editorial choice. Taking the existential additive constant to be a nonnegative integer is equivalent to allowing any real constant by upward rounding and monotonicity of the eligible source class. This does not replace the leading coefficient one by an unspecified multiplicative factor.

Retrieved arXiv:2303.06802v2, verified revision metadata 30 May 2023 against the landing page and PDF, and read Definition 1.1 and the introduction on printed p.1, Theorem 1.6 and Corollary 1.9 on p.6, probability definitions in Section 2, and the explicit additive-threshold open question in Section 8 p.38. Theorem 1.6 is for interleaved independent sources and includes ordinary concatenation. It has an error-dependent multiplicative constant c > 1. Its title and asymptotic optimality do not settle the coefficient-one target. Full proofs of the known constructions were not independently reverified.

The mathematical law ranges over all distributions on a finite binary domain, not just flat or efficient sources. It is explicitly defined by real mass functions. The evaluator receives one pair of strings and the length only. All randomness belongs to the input product distribution. Single-bit statistical distance is exactly the displayed absolute bias; this is not a stronger guarantee conditioned on either source. Vacuous small lengths retain the evaluation clock requirement.

Read arXiv:2404.17013v1, submission 25 April 2024 and title-page date 29 April 2024, introduction and Theorems 1.1–1.4 on printed pp.1–3. Theorem 1.3 requires k >= c log n for c > 1 and gives constant-error one-bit non-malleability. It strengthens a different aspect of the model without claiming log n plus an additive constant. Confirmed ICALP 2024 and FOCS 2023 publication labels from Xin Li’s primary author webpage, accessed 16 September 2026.

Read ECCC TR25-107 revision 3, posted 14 July 2026, abstract and Section 1 through Theorem 1.2 on printed p.4 / PDF p.8. The theorem is conditional on the paper’s hardness assumption and extracts from distributions generated by size n^c circuits; neither condition is present in this card. Confirmed STOC 2026 listing on the official proceedings page and Ronen Shaltiel’s author list. No claim of independently checking all subsequent proofs is made.

Its title page gives revision 18 December 2022, so its pre-2023 introductory state of the art is not treated as a fresh 2025 status certificate. Read the ECCC TR25-108 abstract, 1 August 2025: Aggarwal, Dutta, Mukherjee, Nagargoje and Obremski use a random common reference string and linear min-entropy, a different model. The Cornell February 2026 talk about that construction is not an additive-threshold solution.

This supports a dated source-open classification with a bounded-review limit, not an exhaustive current-open certificate. Existing comments, related identities, score 92 and category are retained.
